div.l: Of which blyth and gladde was eủery wyght/
And tellen forth his tale hit is reson̄
By forward and composicyoun̄
As ye haue herde what nede wordes mo
And when̄ this goode man̄ sawh hit so
As he þat was wyse and obedyent
To kepen̄ his forward by his fre assent
He seyd sythen̄ y schaƚƚlle bygynne the game
What welkome be the cutte on goddes name
Now lete us ryde and herken̄ what y sey
And with þat worde we ryde forth oure wey
And bygan̄ with ryght a mery chere
His tale a non̄e and seyd as ye may here

l.hi: Here endeth þe prolog of þis / Boke

div.l: Here bigynneth the Knyghtꝭes Tale
WHilom̄ as olde storyes telle us ·
There was a Duke hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lord and gouernour
And in his tyme such a conqueroure
That gretter was none vnder sonn̄e
Full many a ryche cuntrey had he wonne ·
What with his wysdom̄ and chyualery
He conquered all the lond of Femynye ·
That whilom̄ was clepud Sythia
And wedded þe quene ypolyta
And brought hur hom̄e in his cuntre
With mych glorye and solempnyte
And eke hur yonge huster Emelye
And þus with victorye and melody
